# Service commands

## Rollout policies and rollback

`ServiceCLI.update` and `Service.update` accept optional update and rollback
policy fields. Each defaults to `None`, leaving the corresponding CLI option
unspecified. Parallelism is an integer from 0 through 2**64 - 1; zero requests
all tasks at once. Delay and monitor accept integer seconds or `timedelta` and
must fit 0 through 2**63 - 1 nanoseconds. They are sent as exact integer
nanoseconds. Maximum failure ratios are finite numbers in [0, 1]; Docker stores
these as float32, so downstream rounding can occur. Update failure actions are
`pause`, `continue`, or `rollback`; rollback actions are `pause` or `continue`.
Both orders are `stop-first` or `start-first`.

`ServiceCLI.rollback` targets one service by name, ID, or handle. Neither
operation probes support or retries a mutation. CLI success is not an
application-health guarantee. If the local command is interrupted, its remote
outcome may be unknown. The operator retains ownership of the service and
cluster; direct service options are separate from policies in stack files.

Syntax references: Docker CLI commit `66786b775ad2f71a4f6de79965a6f3d2efb08852`,
[`opts.go`](https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/66786b775ad2f71a4f6de79965a6f3d2efb08852/cli/command/service/opts.go)
and [`rollback.go`](https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/66786b775ad2f71a4f6de79965a6f3d2efb08852/cli/command/service/rollback.go).
The full set of twelve policy flags has a historical API feature floor of
1.29; standalone rollback is annotated 1.31. These syntax references are not supported-version
qualifications; operators must qualify their own CLI and daemon versions.
